main_claim: Clipping off-policy tokens in SFT reduces forgetting (11.54%) and boosts subsequent RL (7.09%) versus standard SFT.
evidence: ALFWorld and ScienceWorld experiments; latent-space analysis of representational drift.
rationale: Gains are quantified on named benchmarks; assertion that degradation 'primarily results from' off-policy tokens is causal beyond the largely correlational evidence reported.

main_claim: Contrastive RL from a single goal observation yields emergent skills and directed exploration without rewards or demonstrations.
evidence: Qualitative account of a manipulation task; skills emerge before first success; no quantitative results stated.
rationale: 'All You Need' sufficiency claim is broader than example-based evidence; abstract itself is candid about limited understanding.

main_claim: Batch norm reduces adversarial and corruption robustness, via decision-boundary tilting along low-variance input dimensions.
evidence: Five standard datasets with double-digit robustness drops; linear toy model plus nonlinear model experiments.
rationale: Title's hedged causal claim ('a cause') matches controlled comparisons and mechanism; abstract frames mechanism as 'we argue'.

main_claim: Upper and lower bounds on fairness estimation error for models trained on complete cases; first known such results.
evidence: Theoretical bounds plus numerical experiments assessing them.
rationale: Theory-backed, scoped claims; 'first known results' is qualified novelty.

main_claim: Robust overfitting, robustness overestimation and robustness-accuracy trade-off share one common cause: low-quality training samples.
evidence: Data-quality metric; controlled removal experiments 'largely alleviate' problems; datasets and numbers not given.
rationale: Removal only partially alleviates problems, yet abstract asserts a single common cause; title 'Data Quality Matters' is supported.

main_claim: RLHF training on MuseD-generated multi-step deduction data significantly improves logical reasoning in- and out-of-domain.
evidence: Generated training/test data with controllable difficulty; no benchmarks, models or numbers reported.
rationale: 'Significant improvements' asserted with neither quantification nor named evaluation tasks; title's 'step signals' not described in abstract.

main_claim: A semantic loss derived from first principles gives (near-)SOTA semi-supervised classification and better structured prediction.
evidence: Semi-supervised multi-class classification; structured outputs (rankings, shortest paths); no numbers.
rationale: Claims tied to named task types and hedged '(near-)'; 'significantly' unquantified but not beyond stated scope.

main_claim: BOF4 quantizers reduce block-wise quantization error; with OPQ they reach top perplexity among 4-bit block-wise methods.
evidence: Comparisons to NF4 and AF4; theoretical and data-driven optimization shown equivalent; perplexity results, no numbers.
rationale: Superlative scoped to 4-bit block-wise techniques and perplexity; 'Optimal' in title is part of method name reflecting optimization.

main_claim: DBSCAN-based hierarchical point-set framework addresses density sensitivity and is scalable and robust across dimensions.
evidence: Synthetic datasets only; no baselines or numbers reported.
rationale: Results explicitly scoped to synthetic evaluations; real 3D applications framed as future work ('paving the way').

main_claim: GraphNorm, per-graph normalization with learnable shift, speeds GNN convergence and improves generalization.
evidence: Preconditioning theory; faster convergence than BatchNorm etc.; better graph classification benchmark results.
rationale: Theory and benchmark evidence support 'principled' and 'accelerating'; claims stay within reported scope.

main_claim: EWoK learns robust policies by estimating the worst-case kernel, scaling online RMDPs to high-dimensional domains.
evidence: Cartpole, MinAtar and DeepMind Control Suite experiments.
rationale: 'Any off-the-shelf algorithm' is a design property; effectiveness claims scoped to named environments.

main_claim: ProbGAN learns a generator distribution with data-faithful equilibrium and outperforms multi-generator and probabilistic GANs.
evidence: Theoretical analysis; synthetic multimodal data, CIFAR-10, STL-10, ImageNet.
rationale: 'First' claim is specific and theory-backed; superiority scoped to named datasets and baseline families.

main_claim: BayesAdapter turns pretrained networks into BNNs via cheap Bayesian fine-tuning with competitive accuracy and calibrated uncertainty.
evidence: Experiments on unnamed 'diverse, challenging benchmarks'; qualitative descriptors, no numbers.
rationale: Results described modestly ('satisfactory', 'competitive'); 'to the masses' is motivation, not a reported result.

main_claim: Tiny random feature subsets match or beat full and published selected feature sets, undermining feature-importance claims.
evidence: 30 datasets (RNA-Seq, mass spectrometry, imaging); random subsets match/outperform in 27 of 30.
rationale: Solid evidence base, but 'any arbitrary set is as good as any other' and claims about many FS papers exceed 30 datasets.

main_claim: Spatiotemporal contrastive learning on street view imagery significantly outperforms supervised and unsupervised baselines on urban tasks.
evidence: Place recognition, socioeconomic estimation, perception tasks; no datasets or numbers given.
rationale: 'Significantly outperforms' is unquantified with unnamed datasets; title generic but abstract covers several urban tasks.

main_claim: Learning-from-reversal with differentiable simulation and imitation learning pioneers a paradigm shift, outperforming competitors in insertion.
evidence: Simulated dataset of shapes, materials, containers; unspecified evaluations of sample efficiency, performance, sim-to-real.
rationale: 'Pioneers a paradigm shift' and 'innovative' are sweeping; superiority claims lack any stated scope or numbers.

main_claim: Jointly training streaming and full-context ASR with shared weights improves streaming latency and accuracy, reaching SOTA.
evidence: ContextNet and Conformer on LibriSpeech and MultiDomain; ablation studies.
rationale: SOTA claim scoped to two named datasets and two networks; applicability claim matches tested architecture families.

main_claim: Exploiting laziness and Jacobian low-rankness enables scalable backpropagation-free gradient descent for over-parameterized models.
evidence: Scalable laziness and low-rank measurements; unspecified empirical results.
rationale: Claims modest and conditional ('in cases of massive parameter sharing'); 'opening new pathways' is forward-looking.

main_claim: Tested LLMs show surprisingly high retrieval robustness, but imperfect robustness limits full RAG benefits.
evidence: 1500-question benchmark, 11 LLMs, 3 prompting strategies, three robustness metrics.
rationale: Findings explicitly scoped to the evaluated LLMs ('all of these LLMs'); no claims beyond the study.

main_claim: VLMs behave like bags-of-words on ARO; retrieval shortcuts may explain it; composition-aware negatives help.
evidence: ARO benchmark (50k+ cases); retrieval-without-order experiments; hard-negative mining results; no numbers.
rationale: Causal explanation explicitly hedged ('hypothesize'); claims tied to new benchmark; title is a question.

main_claim: Fine-tuning an LLM to follow annotation guidelines (GoLLIE) improves zero-shot extraction on unseen IE tasks.
evidence: Unspecified 'comprehensive evaluation' against previous zero-shot IE; ablation on guideline detail.
rationale: Title claim matches abstract finding and ablation; comparisons unquantified but not extended beyond zero-shot IE.

main_claim: SAP learns task-agnostic priors from imperfect off-policy data and sparse rewards, enabling zero-shot planning.
evidence: Outperforms baselines on gridworld, robotics tasks and video games.
rationale: 'Wide range' backed by three named domain types; outperformance hedged with 'can'.

main_claim: Dual VQ codebooks in graph contrastive learning may yield more robust features; competitive performance is planned.
evidence: No results reported; authors 'plan to demonstrate' competitive performance on benchmarks.
rationale: Title asserts two codebooks beat one; abstract only posits benefits and plans experiments targeting merely 'competitive' results.

main_claim: Gaussian-smoothed Q-values satisfy a Bellman equation and allow learning Gaussian policy mean and covariance.
evidence: Derivations (Bellman equation, gradient/Hessian relations); standard continuous control benchmarks.
rationale: Theoretical results stated; 'strong results on standard benchmarks' is modest and scoped.

main_claim: FCVL's frequency augmentation and cross-view consistency achieve best single-source generalization for BEV 3D detection.
evidence: Augmentation-graph theory; 'extensive experiments' on unnamed test domains; no numbers.
rationale: 'First study' qualified ('to the best of our knowledge'); best-performance claim scoped to single-source setting.

main_claim: MEDL with adversarial debiasing improves fairness (up to 86%) while preserving performance on clustered data.
evidence: Three datasets (two census/finance classification, one healthcare regression); per-attribute fairness gains.
rationale: Title's out-of-distribution claim is not reported in abstract; 'agnostic to dataset type and task' generalizes from three datasets.

main_claim: Complementary modality information improves VLM answers and reasoning; contradictory information harms performance and confidence.
evidence: SI-VQA dataset; benchmark of several VLMs (PaliGemma, LLaVA); attention analysis; ISI tool.
rationale: Findings scoped to evaluated VLMs and new dataset; 'sets the foundation' is mild rhetoric, not beyond evidence.

main_claim: FL with user-level DP for transformer ASR is achievable with 1.3-4.6% absolute WER degradation.
evidence: Studies of architecture, seeds, heterogeneity, cohort size; per-layer clipping; DP results extrapolated to population scale.
rationale: Quantified results with extrapolation stated; 'first baselines' qualified by 'not aware of prior work'.

main_claim: Supervised and self-supervised reblurring losses improve perceptual quality of deblurred images.
evidence: Large-scale benchmarks and real images; NIQE, LPIPS and visual sharpness.
rationale: Title's assertion is the design premise the abstract explains; perceptual-quality claims scoped to stated metrics.

main_claim: Beam search degradation arises from early highly non-greedy decisions; constraining them eliminates degradation.
evidence: Empirical study on three sequence synthesis tasks; two constrained-search methods evaluated.
rationale: Title qualifies 'unconstrained'; claims tied to three tasks; 'effectively eliminates' strong but within tested scope.

main_claim: Disentangling goal and framing in LLM activations enables state-of-the-art PAIR jailbreak detection, up to +21 points.
evidence: PAIR+Framing dataset; ReDAct and FrameShield; various LLM families; theoretical separation guarantees.
rationale: Title's absolute 'can't hide' exceeds accuracy gains; conclusion generalizes from PAIR detection to adversarial prompts broadly and interpretability.

main_claim: Constraining offline GFlowNets away from unsupported flows yields higher-scoring and diverse candidates.
evidence: Experiments on 'several widely-used datasets' (unnamed); no numbers.
rationale: Title claim matches abstract's stated results; abstract wording is modest ('validate the effectiveness').

main_claim: BagNet, a bag-of-local-features ResNet variant, reaches high ImageNet accuracy and behaves like standard DNNs.
evidence: 87.6% top-5 with 32px patches; comparisons with VGG-16, ResNet-152, DenseNet-169 on sensitivity, errors, interactions.
rationale: Title scoped to ImageNet and backed by numbers; broad historical interpretation hedged with 'suggests'.

main_claim: Learned divisive normalization improves AlexNet accuracy by 1-2 points, most when combined with canonical normalization.
evidence: AlexNet on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet; comparisons with batch/group/layer norm; manifold, sparsity, RF analyses.
rationale: Title explicitly scoped to AlexNet; numeric gains reported; mechanism statements describe observed correlates.

main_claim: Pixel-wise, gradient-free ablation CAM produces qualitatively and quantitatively superior explanation maps.
evidence: Experiments with newly proposed adversarial-attack-based metrics; no datasets or numbers.
rationale: Superiority asserted without detail, but absence of numbers alone is not overreach; title is a design slogan.

main_claim: Contrastive pre-training yields dense retrievers competitive with BM25 unsupervised and SOTA on BEIR after fine-tuning.
evidence: BEIR benchmark; comparisons with BM25 and BERT pre-training; few-shot setting; MS-MARCO fine-tuning.
rationale: Claims carefully scoped ('competitive', 'many domains', named benchmark).

main_claim: Multi-task MLM/TLM training on clusters of similar African languages strongly boosts within-cluster translation.
evidence: New parallel dataset; similarity metric; +29 BLEU on Bafia-Ewondo versus prior methods.
rationale: Title targets African languages broadly; abstract evidence is one language cluster with a single highlighted pair.

main_claim: Linking GAMs and SHAP enables training purified GAMs that compute Shapley values in one forward pass.
evidence: Variational perspective; theoretical results on GAM representation limits; no empirical results mentioned.
rationale: 'Deep insights into nearly all recent developments' is sweeping beyond reported analysis; core method claim matches title.

main_claim: The STAR gated cell preserves gradient magnitude, enabling substantially deeper multi-layer RNNs with better performance.
evidence: Gradient propagation analysis; five sequence modelling tasks on three datasets.
rationale: Title's 'can be trained' supported by analysis and multi-task experiments; claims stay within reported scope.

main_claim: MaskCLR's targeted masking and multi-level contrastive learning consistently outperform SOTA in accuracy and robustness.
evidence: NTU60, NTU120, Kinetics400; standard and perturbed skeletons; single encoder (ST-MHSA).
rationale: SOTA scoped to named benchmarks, but 'seamlessly incorporated into transformer-based models' generalizes from one encoder.

main_claim: NNGeometry provides a simple PyTorch interface for FIM and NTK linear-algebra operations on practical networks.
evidence: Library description, design motivation, demonstration on deep networks.
rationale: Descriptive tool paper; 'Easy and Fast' are design attributes plausibly backed by simple interface and approximations.

main_claim: GLOBE-CE improves scalability of global counterfactual explanations, with speed, reliability and interpretability gains.
evidence: Real-world datasets and user studies; mathematical analysis of categorical feature translations.
rationale: Title asserts a universal reliability-efficiency trade-off; abstract reports no such result and claims its method improves both.

main_claim: Tree-structured VAE matches autoregressive log-likelihood with sequential computation proportional to tree depth.
evidence: One synthetic dataset and one automated theorem proving dataset.
rationale: Modest, scoped claim ('similar' likelihood) on two stated datasets.

main_claim: FOND achieves state-of-the-art domain generalization for domain-linked classes given enough domain-shared classes.
evidence: Experiments with baselines across popular DG tasks; theoretical and practical insights.
rationale: SOTA claim explicitly conditioned on sufficient domain-shared classes; benchmarks unnamed but no broad generalization.

main_claim: IRIS, a Transformer world-model agent, sets Atari 100k state of the art among methods without lookahead.
evidence: Atari 100k: mean human-normalized score 1.046; superhuman on 10 of 26 games.
rationale: Abstract is precise and scoped; title generalizes to Transformers as world models from one agent on one benchmark.

main_claim: Architecture matters for scaling behaviour, and the best-performing model changes across scales.
evidence: Systematic study of ten architectures, upstream pretraining and downstream transfer.
rationale: Findings scoped to ten architectures; implications hedged with 'we believe'.

main_claim: Adapting transformer-based trackers to class-agnostic counting achieves new state-of-the-art results.
evidence: MixFormer and TransT adaptations; FSC-147 and CARPK; ablation studies.
rationale: 'Strong baselines' supported by SOTA on named datasets; 'Count Everything' reflects the class-agnostic task definition.

main_claim: code2seq, attending over AST paths, outperforms code-specific models and state-of-the-art NMT models.
evidence: Two tasks, two programming languages, four datasets up to 16M examples.
rationale: 'Significantly outperforms' is unquantified but scoped to stated tasks and datasets.

main_claim: SEARNN's global-local losses improve RNN training over maximum likelihood.
evidence: OCR, spelling correction, and machine translation with subsampling.
rationale: Improvement claims tied to named tasks; no generalization beyond them.

main_claim: Character-level seq2seq normalizes Amharic non-standard words with 94.8% accuracy.
evidence: Single accuracy figure; data resources unspecified.
rationale: Result framed cautiously ('promising given the resource we use'); descriptive method paper.
